name: Kalioop – Class & Event Registration with Seat Limits
author: Streetcar Productions

sections.description:
Kalioop helps a school, studio, club or any organizer run classes and events with limited seats. You create activities with scheduled sessions, people register for them, and you see exactly who is coming.

What you can do

  • Activities and sessions. Each activity has any number of sessions. Each session has its own time zone, capacity, registration window and a manual “close registration” switch. Availability is always clear: available, not yet open, registration closed, manually closed, sold out or completed.
  • Free registration. Add the Kalioop Registration block to a page and choose the activity by name, or put the shortcode [kalioop_registration] on a page. Visitors choose sessions and register one or more people, with or without an account. Capacity is checked under a database lock, so a full session cannot be overbooked.
  • Paid registration with WooCommerce (optional). Link a session to a WooCommerce simple product. Buyers choose who is attending on the product page, seats are held for 30 minutes by default while they check out, and each seat is confirmed when the order is paid. Works with the classic checkout and the Cart and Checkout blocks, and with High-Performance Order Storage. A screen lists paid orders whose seats need your attention.
  • Rosters. Administrators can download a CSV roster for one session or a whole activity. It lists confirmed registrations only; a separate, clearly labeled download can also list people who have not paid yet. It includes every signup question people answered, including questions you have since removed or reworded. Under Registrations, the Past list can be narrowed by activity and by a first and last day, so an older roster is easy to find. Names that start with a spreadsheet formula character are neutralized so a spreadsheet will not run them.
  • Add someone yourself. On a session’s roster, Add attendee registers a person, for example someone who signed up by phone: they take a normal seat and the roster shows they were added by staff. For a session sold through WooCommerce the button is Add complimentary seat: it uses a seat without creating an order or taking a payment.
  • Duplicate. Start a new class from an existing one with Duplicate on the Activities list, or repeat a date with Duplicate on the Sessions list. Nothing is saved until you choose Create the copy. A copied activity starts with no sessions and a copied session starts with an empty roster; the original keeps its bookings.
  • Attendance. Mark each confirmed seat attended or no-show, correct it, or reset it. Attendance is recorded separately and never changes a registration, its seat, capacity, payment or an order.
  • Confirmation emails (best effort). For a free registration form, one email per submission goes to the address a new guest typed on the form, or to a signed-in member’s account address; a guest who gave no address gets none. For paid seats, one email per paid order goes to the order’s billing address. A repeat or a retry does not send it twice, and a failed send never undoes a registration. Emails use WordPress’s own mail function, so delivery depends on your site’s email setup and is not guaranteed.

Paid seats: what has been tested

Payments are handled by WooCommerce and your payment gateway. Kalioop does not need any particular gateway and does not require Stripe. Tested: WooCommerce 11.2 with the official WooCommerce Stripe Payment Gateway in Stripe’s test (sandbox) mode, in the classic checkout and the Cart and Checkout blocks: card payments, 3-D Secure (completed and failed), declined cards, full, partial and per-seat refunds, repeated and out-of-order webhook messages, and several buyers competing for the last seat. Not verified: other gateways, delayed or bank-based payment methods such as direct debit, disputes, manual capture and express-checkout buttons. No live payment has been made in testing. Please test your own gateway and payment methods with test orders before taking real bookings.

Privacy, cookies and external services

  • Kalioop makes no requests to any external service and loads no remote scripts, fonts or styles. WooCommerce and your payment gateway, if you use them, are separate software with their own behavior.
  • It stores people’s first and last names, an optional email address, registration and attendance records, an audit trail of what happened to each registration, and the answers given to any extra questions you add under Settings (stored with the question’s wording, one set of answers per seat), in its own database tables. WordPress’s personal data export includes those answers. Guests who give no email address are supported. With WooCommerce, billing details stay in WooCommerce.
  • Cookies are set only for visitors who use the registration or seat-selection forms, and are HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax and Secure on HTTPS. kalio_guest is set when a guest first registers or saves people to buy a seat; it holds a signed token that lets that browser see and cancel its own registrations and lasts 7 days. kalio_guest_link is set when a guest opens a private link from an email (a guest who gave an address can ask for one); the link is valid for 3 days and so is the cookie. kalio_draft is a random binding cookie, set when a form is shown again after an error or a change of page so typed names are not lost; it lasts up to 10 minutes, the saved entries it points to are kept for 5 minutes, and they never include an email address. No cookie is set for visitors who do not use these forms.
  • Email is sent through WordPress’s own mail function: a confirmation, and a private link if a guest asks for one.
  • The WordPress personal data export and erase tools (Tools > Export Personal Data and Erase Personal Data) include Kalioop’s people. Nothing is deleted automatically. Deleting a WordPress user does not delete that user’s saved people in Kalioop; use Erase Personal Data for that.
  • Exported rosters contain names, any stored emails and the answers to your signup questions, including questions you have since removed: keep them private.
  • This readme is not legal advice. Check what your own use requires.

Limits to know about

  • Single-site WordPress only. Network activation is refused and multisite is not supported.
  • It needs MySQL 8.0 or newer, or MariaDB 10.6 or newer, and refuses to save data on an older database.
  • Sessions sold through WooCommerce product variations are not supported yet; link a session to a simple product.
  • Kalioop does not refund or cancel payments for you. Cancelling a seat frees it; refunds are made in WooCommerce (a refund of a whole order frees all its seats; refunding one seat line frees that seat).
  • If you use a page cache or CDN, exclude the page with the registration block or shortcode; the pages that show people or seats are sent as uncacheable. Behavior behind a real CDN has not been tested.
  • Tested on WordPress 7.0 and 7.1, PHP 8.1, 8.2, 8.3 and 8.4, MySQL 8.0 and 8.4, MariaDB 10.6 and 12.3, and WooCommerce 11.2 and 11.3 (optional). Other versions are untested.

WooCommerce and Stripe are trademarks of their respective owners. Kalioop is not affiliated with or endorsed by them.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install it from the Plugins screen, and activate it on an individual site (not network-wide).
  2. Open the Kalioop menu. Under Activities, create an activity; under Sessions, add its sessions with a time zone, capacity and registration window.
  3. For free registration, add the Kalioop Registration block to a page and choose the activity by name, or add the shortcode [kalioop_registration] (add activity="ID" to list only one activity).
  4. For paid seats, set up WooCommerce and a payment gateway, then enter a price per seat on the activity. Kalioop creates a simple product and links the activity’s sessions to it. You can also link your own simple product from the session’s edit screen. Buyers choose a session on the product page.
  5. Under Sessions, choose View roster next to a session to see who registered, mark attendance and download the CSV. For a completed session, open the Past tab. On a roster, choose Add attendee to register someone yourself. To find an older roster, open Registrations, choose Past and filter by activity and date.

Requirements: WordPress 7.0 or newer, PHP 8.1 or newer, MySQL 8.0 or newer or MariaDB 10.6 or newer. WooCommerce is optional: everything except paid seats works without it.
sections.faq:
Can I set up a paid class from the WooCommerce product screen?

Yes. On a simple product, use the Kalioop Sessions box: tick “Sell this product as a Kalioop class”, click Update, then add the dates and seats. The price stays in WooCommerce. Administrators only for now.

What happens if I delete or unpublish the product for a paid class?

The session stays paid and is paused. It cannot be registered for free, and its page says booking is not available right now. Restore or replace the product, or open the session and tick “Make this session free” if it should now be free. Leaving the product box empty does not make a session free.

Can I add someone myself, for example a phone signup?

Yes. Open the session’s roster and choose Add attendee. Enter their name, an optional email and the answers to your signup questions; they are registered at once and the roster marks them as added by staff. If the session is sold through WooCommerce the button is Add complimentary seat: it uses one seat and creates no order and no payment. You cannot add someone to a full, closed or finished session from there; the page says why.

Can I reuse a class or a date?

Yes. Choose Duplicate on the Activities list to start a new class from an existing one, or Duplicate on the Sessions list to repeat a date. The form opens filled in and nothing is saved until you choose Create the copy. A copied session needs its own start and end times and the registration window is not copied. A copy of a paid session keeps its product; if that product no longer exists, name a working product or choose to make the copy free.

Do I need WooCommerce?

No. Activities, sessions, free registration, rosters, attendance and confirmation emails work without it. WooCommerce is only needed to sell seats.

Do I need Stripe?

No. Stripe is optional. Other WooCommerce payment gateways and methods work through WooCommerce, but the only one tested here is the official WooCommerce Stripe gateway in test mode (see Description). Test your own gateway and payment methods with test orders before taking real bookings.

Can visitors register without an account?

Yes. A guest registers one or more people without an account. A signed cookie lets that browser see and cancel its own registrations for 7 days; a guest who gave an email address can ask for a private link to return later (valid for 3 days).

Can I export a list of who is coming?

Yes. Under Registrations, choose a session and use the CSV download. It lists confirmed people only unless you choose the separate download that also lists people who have not paid yet; those rows are marked as not confirmed.

Does it send emails?

Yes, best effort: one confirmation per free registration submission (only if a guest typed an address, or a signed-in member registers) and one per paid order, plus a private link if a guest asks for one. It uses WordPress’s own mail function, so delivery depends on your site’s email setup and is not guaranteed.

Does it contact any outside service?

No. Kalioop makes no external requests.

What happens to my data if I delete the plugin?

Nothing, unless you enable “Delete all Kalioop data when the plugin is deleted” in Kalioop > Settings first.

Can I set a limit on how many people can join?

Yes. Every session has its own capacity. When it is full, registration for that session closes, and the session shows as sold out. You can also close a session by hand at any time, and set when registration opens and closes.

Can one person register several people for several sessions at once?

Yes. On the registration form, add each person and tick the sessions they will attend. Each person gets their own seat in each session they choose, in one submission. If the sessions are paid, it is one checkout.

What happens if someone cancels?

Cancelling a seat frees it for someone else. Kalioop does not refund payments for you: for a paid seat, make the refund in WooCommerce. Refunding a whole order frees all its seats, and refunding one seat line frees that seat.

Is there a waitlist?

Not yet. A full session shows as sold out and closes to new registrations.

Will it work with a caching plugin or CDN?

Kalioop sends the pages that show people or seats as uncacheable, but it has not been tested behind a real CDN. If you use a page cache or CDN, exclude the page that has the registration block or shortcode.

Does it work on WordPress multisite?

No. Kalioop supports single-site WordPress only, and network activation is refused.

Where are the translations?

Kalioop is translation-ready (text domain kalioop). Translations from translate.wordpress.org load automatically when they exist.
sections.changelog:
1.2.3

  • Readme update only: six new answers in the FAQ (seat limits, registering several people for several sessions, cancellations and refunds, waitlist, caching and CDN, multisite). No code changes.

1.2.2

  • Now works on PHP 8.1 and WordPress 7.0 (previously PHP 8.2 and WordPress 7.1 were required). The full test suite passes on both.
  • If a database update fails with an error message containing invalid characters, the message is now still recorded and shown on older WordPress versions.

1.2.1

  • Listing update only: a clearer plugin name and description (Class & Event Registration with Seat Limits) and updated search tags. No code changes.

1.2.0

  • Add attendee: staff can register a person from a session’s roster (for example a phone signup). They take a normal seat and the roster shows they were added by staff. On a session sold through WooCommerce the button is Add complimentary seat: it uses a seat and creates no order or payment.
  • Duplicate an activity or a session from their lists. The form opens filled in and nothing is saved until you choose Create the copy; a copied activity has no sessions and a copied session has an empty roster. A copy keeps free or paid as the original, and a paid original whose product is gone needs a working product or an explicit “Make this copy free”.
  • Find past rosters: under Registrations > Past, filter by activity and by an inclusive range of each session’s local start date.
  • Roster CSVs now include every signup answer in the export, including questions you have since removed or reworded.
  • New Kalioop Registration block for the page editor: choose an activity by name. It shows the same registration form as the shortcode, which keeps working.
  • A refreshed, consistent look across the Dashboard (with a Booking paused state and a database check that runs itself), Activities, Sessions, Registrations, Settings and a task-first Help guide, with the Kalioop mark.
  • A clearer price field on activities, a polished Kalioop Sessions box on the WooCommerce product screen, and a Kalioop column on the WooCommerce Products list.
  • On a roster, the Edit name popover closes when you click outside it or press Escape.

1.1.0

  • A paid session stays paid. Deleting, trashing or unpublishing its product no longer turns the session free: it is paused (booking says it is not available right now) until you restore or replace the product, or tick “Make this session free”. An empty product box never removes a link.
  • Set up a paid class from the WooCommerce product screen: a new Kalioop Sessions box on simple products adds and edits the class sessions. Administrators only.
  • Needs attention now flags paid sessions that lost their product link, and linked products with no price, a price of 0, no stock or that need shipping. The Sessions list shows paused sessions.
  • Product variations can no longer be newly linked (they cannot be booked).
  • The View roster link on the Sessions list is a larger touch target.
  • On the registration form, a saved person who already holds a seat in a session is greyed out for it and marked “Already registered”.

1.0.0

  • First public release: activities and sessions, free registration for guests and members, capacity under database locks, optional paid seats through WooCommerce (classic checkout and blocks), an administrator review of paid orders, CSV rosters, per-seat attendance and confirmation emails.
